mismatch.message: simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_slee()

summary: The AD_SLEE dispatcher arm stops at a missing uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_slee() implementation during a landed monster attack against the hero. The whole source function has three attacker/defender branches; this case reaches its monster-to-hero branch, where C prints the hit message and its recorded rn2(5) value of 3 fails the effect gate. This case therefore establishes the missing function and continuation boundary, not an actual sleep effect.

source.branch: Port all of mhitm_ad_slee(): hero attacking a non-sleeping monster applies the source magic-cancellation and sleep_monst gates; a monster attacking the hero prints hitmsg, then applies its gm.multi >= 0, !rn2(5), and magic-cancellation gates, recording or clearing seen sleep resistance and falling asleep only when each gate permits; monster-versus-monster attacks use the two short-circuit sleep_monst calls, optional visible message, STRAT_WAITFORU clear, and slept_monst. The assigned recording reaches the monster-to-hero arm, but rn2(5)=3 fails the effect gate.
callers: uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() dispatches AD_SLEE to mhitm_ad_slee(); js/uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping() currently maps AD_SLEE to the unported-operation stop.
mhitu.c:hitmu() calls mhitm_adtyping(mtmp, mattk, &gy.youmonst, &mhm); js/mhitu.js:hitmu() invokes the same dispatcher for the assigned monster-to-hero path.
uhitm.c:damageum() calls mhitm_adtyping(&gy.youmonst, mattk, mdef, &mhm); js/uhitm.js:damageum() is the hero-to-monster production route.
mhitm.c:mdamagem() calls mhitm_adtyping(magr, mattk, mdef, &mhm); js/mhitm.js:mdamagem() is the monster-to-monster production route.
dependencies: mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() -> boolean, consumed as a gate in the hero-to-monster and monster-to-hero arms; its result depends on magic_negation() -> MC integer and rn2(10) when the attacker is not canceled. Existing JS implementations are js/uhitm.js:mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() and js/mhitu.js:magic_negation().
sleep_monst() -> boolean, consumed by short-circuit conditions in the hero-to-monster and monster-to-monster arms; C source is mhitm.c:1221-1245 and JS implementation is js/mhitm.js:sleep_monst().
rn2(5) supplies the monster-to-hero effect gate and rnd(10) supplies sleep duration; preserve source ordering and short-circuit behavior.

hitmsg(), monstseesu(), monstunseesu(), fall_asleep(), and slept_monst() have void message/state effects in their respective branches; their current JS implementations are present in js/mhitu.js, js/mondata.js, js/timeout.js, and js/mhitm.js.

evidence: At examined commit 04b79edc2bcff3a4c2d70efba937608818f85b53, the upstream submodule is pinned at 16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4. In uhitm.c:3478-3521, mhitm_ad_slee() has three complete arms selected by whether magr or mdef is gy.youmonst; its monster-to-hero arm calls hitmsg before testing gm.multi >= 0, !rn2(5), and !mhitm_mgc_atk_negated(). If the hero resists sleep it calls monstseesu(M_SEEN_SLEEP) and returns; otherwise it calls monstunseesu(), fall_asleep(-rnd(10), TRUE), and prints the sleep message.

The saved C recording at step 33 has key ".", the bite screen, and the source gate call rn2(5)=3 @ mhitm_ad_slee(uhitm.c:3495). The source condition is !rn2(5), so this attempt fails before magic cancellation or the resistance/sleep effects; the private step excerpt is .cache/v18-investigations/wizard-hostile-homunculus-ad-slee-c59/c-step-33.json.

The current saved queue/evaluation entry identifies 2 unmatched screens out of 35 and a step-33 stop requiring uhitm.c mhitm_ad_slee(). The stop is the actual cause: at js/uhitm.js:4837 the AD_SLEE case calls unported(), while uhitm.c:4816 dispatches to mhitm_ad_slee().

The direct dispatcher callers are uhitm.c:4854 damageum(), mhitu.c:1191 hitmu(), and mhitm.c:1059 mdamagem(); their current JS counterparts call js/uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping() at js/uhitm.js:4886, js/mhitu.js:1707, and js/mhitm.js:1057. Their JS implementations exist in js/uhitm.js:776, js/mhitu.js:1566, and js/mhitm.js:184; preserve the boolean values, ordered rolls, and short-circuit behavior in the new source function.
